pois.name: Polly Woodside
pois.intro: Polly Woodside is a three-masted, iron-hulled barque, preserved in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, and forming the central feature of the South Wharf precinct. The ship was originally built in Belfast by William J. Woodside and was launched in 1885.

pois.name: Cooks' Cottage
pois.description: Family cottage constructed in 1755 in the village of Great Ayton, North Yorkshire, UK by Captain James Cook's parents. Transported to Melbourne in 1934. Source: Wikipedia
pois.intro: Cooks' Cottage, also known as Captain Cook's Cottage, is located in the Fitzroy Gardens, Melbourne, Australia. The cottage was constructed in 1755 in the English village of Great Ayton, North Yorkshire, by the parents of Captain James Cook, James and Grace Cook.

pois.name: Beef House
pois.intro: 380 Melbourne is a residential and hotel skyscraper in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Designed by Elenberg Fraser and developed by Brady Group, the project includes 728 residential apartments as well as 312 hotel rooms within a 67-level skyscraper, and reaches a height of 217.5 metres.

pois.description: Pop-up cafe kiosk offering quick grab & go selection with very friendly and fast service

pois.name: Royal Exhibition Building
pois.intro: The Royal Exhibition Building is a UNESCO World Heritage-listed building in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, built in 1879–1880 as part of the international exhibition movement, which presented over 50 exhibitions between 1851 and 1915 around the globe. The building sits on approximately 26 hectares, is 150 metres long and is surrounded by four city streets.

pois.name: Carlton Gardens
pois.intro: The Carlton Gardens is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located on the northeastern edge of the Central Business District in the suburb of Carlton, Melbourne, in the state of Victoria, Australia. The gardens are a popular picnic and barbecue area, and are home to an array of wildlife, including brushtail possums.

pois.name: National Gallery of Victoria
pois.intro: The National Gallery of Victoria, popularly known as the NGV, is an art museum in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Founded in 1861, it is Australia's oldest and most visited art museum.

pois.name: Melbourne Museum
pois.intro: The Melbourne Museum is a natural and cultural history museum located in the Carlton Gardens in Melbourne, Australia. Located adjacent to the Royal Exhibition Building, the museum was opened in 2000 as a project of the Government of Victoria, on behalf of Museums Victoria which administers the venue.

pois.name: Melbourne Zoological Gardens
pois.intro: Melbourne Zoo is a zoo in Melbourne, Australia. It is located within Royal Park in Parkville, approximately 4 kilometres north of the centre of Melbourne.

pois.name: Federation Square
pois.intro: Federation Square is a venue for arts, culture and public events on the edge of the Melbourne central business district. It covers an area of 3.2 ha at the intersection of Flinders and Swanston Streets built above busy railway lines and across the road from Flinders Street station.

pois.name: Shrine of Remembrance
pois.intro: The Shrine of Remembrance is a war memorial in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, located in Kings Domain on St Kilda Road. It was built to honour the men and women of Victoria who served in World War I, but now functions as a memorial to all Australians who have served in any war.

pois.name: Crown Melbourne
pois.intro: Crown Melbourne is an integrated resort consisting of a casino and hotel located on the south bank of the Yarra River, in Melbourne, Australia. Crown Melbourne is a subsidiary of Crown Resorts, and was the first casino of the now-international Crown brand.

pois.name: Australian Centre for Contemporary Art
pois.intro: The Australian Centre For Contemporary Art is a contemporary art gallery in Melbourne, Australia. The gallery is located on Sturt Street in the Melbourne Arts Precinct, in the inner suburb of Southbank.

pois.name: Immigration Museum
pois.intro: The Immigration Museum is a culture museum that focuses on the immigration history of Melbourne and Victoria. Opened in 1998 as a division of Museums Victoria, Immigration Museum is located at the restored Customs House building on Flinders Street, in the city centre of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia.

pois.name: Queen Victoria Market
pois.intro: The Queen Victoria Market is a major landmark and public marketplace in the central business district of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Covering over seven hectares, it is the largest open air market in the Southern Hemisphere.

pois.name: Old Melbourne Observatory
pois.intro: Melbourne Observatory is an observatory located on a hill adjacent to the Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria. The observatory commenced operations in 1863 and was decommissioned from official Government work in 1945.

pois.name: Old Melbourne Gaol
pois.description: Closed prison, now a museum and tourist attraction.
pois.intro: The Old Melbourne Gaol is a former jail and current museum on Russell Street, in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. It consists of a bluestone building and courtyard, and is located next to the old City Police Watch House and City Courts buildings, and opposite the Russell Street Police Headquarters.

pois.name: Luna Park
pois.intro: Luna Park Melbourne is a historic amusement park located on the foreshore of Port Phillip Bay in St Kilda, Melbourne, Victoria. It opened on 13 December 1912, with a formal opening a week later, and has been operating almost continuously ever since.

pois.name: Arts Centre Melbourne
pois.intro: Arts Centre Melbourne, originally known as the Victorian Arts Centre and briefly called the Arts Centre, is a performing arts centre consisting of a complex of theatres and concert halls in the Melbourne Arts Precinct, located in the central Melbourne suburb of Southbank in Victoria, Australia.

pois.name: ACMI
pois.intro: ACMI, formerly the Australian Centre for the Moving Image, is Australia's national museum of screen culture including film, television, videogames, digital culture and art. ACMI was established in 2002 and is based at Federation Square in Melbourne, Victoria.

pois.name: Hellenic Museum
pois.intro: The Hellenic Museum is an art and history museum in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia promoting Hellenic culture, both ancient and contemporary, through programs, exhibitions and events. The museum also covers the Greek community of Melbourne and Australia.

pois.name: Scienceworks
pois.intro: Scienceworks is one of Australia’s leading science museums located in Spotswood, a suburb of Melbourne, Victoria. It is one of three museums operated by Museums Victoria.

pois.name: Ian Potter Centre: NGV Australia
pois.intro: The Ian Potter Centre: NGV Australia is an art gallery that houses the Australian part of the art collection of the National Gallery of Victoria. The Ian Potter Centre: NGV Australia is located at Federation Square in Melbourne, Victoria; while the gallery's international works are displayed at the NGV International on St Kilda Road.

pois.name: Newport Railway Museum
pois.intro: The Newport Railway Museum is located on Champion Road, Newport, Victoria, near the North Williamstown station.

pois.name: Chinese Museum
pois.intro: The Chinese Museum or Museum of Chinese Australian History is an Australian history museum located in Melbourne's Chinatown. The museum was established in 1985 with a charter to present the history of Australians of Chinese ancestry, and is dedicated to documenting, preserving and displaying the history, heritage and culture of Australia's Chinese community.

pois.name: The Australian Sports Museum
pois.intro: The Australian Sports Museum, formerly the National Sports Museum, is a museum dedicated to Australian sport and is located within the Melbourne Cricket Ground in Melbourne, Australia. There are exhibits for sports such as cricket, Australian rules football, the Summer and Winter Olympic Games, tennis, rugby league, rugby union, soccer, basketball, boxing and netball.

pois.name: Grainger Museum
pois.intro: The Grainger Museum is a repository of items documenting the life, career and music of the composer, folklorist, educator and pianist Percy Grainger (b. Melbourne, 1882; d.

pois.name: Young & Jacksons
pois.intro: Young and Jackson is a hotel in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, at the corner of Flinders Street and Swanston Street. Established in 1861, it is listed on the Victorian Heritage Register.

pois.name: Block Arcade
pois.intro: The Block Arcade is a historic shopping arcade in the central business district of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Constructed between 1891 and 1893, it is considered one of the late Victorian era's finest shopping arcades and ranks among Melbourne's most popular tourist attractions.

pois.name: South Melbourne Market
pois.intro: The South Melbourne Market is a covered food and general goods market located in South Melbourne, Victoria. Opened in 1867, it is the oldest continuously operating market in Melbourne.

pois.name: Jam Factory
pois.intro: The Jam Factory was a shopping and entertainment centre, located in Chapel Street, South Yarra, a suburb of Melbourne, Australia. The Jam Factory is owned by Newmark Capital.

pois.name: All Star Comics
pois.intro: All Star Comics Melbourne is an Australian comic book store co-owned by Mitchell Davies and Troy Varker. The store was first opened in February 2011 and in 2014, won the Spirit of Comics Retailer Award at the 26th annual Eisner Awards.

pois.name: Prahran Market
pois.intro: Prahran Market is a food market in South Yarra, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Located on Commercial Road near Chapel Street, it was established in neighbouring Prahran in the 1860s, before moving to its present location in 1881.

pois.name: Albert Park
pois.intro: Albert Park is a 225-hectare urban park, freshwater artificial lake and sports venue, located in the eponymous inner-city suburb of Melbourne, in Victoria, Australia.

pois.name: Royal Botanic Gardens
pois.intro: The Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria are botanic gardens across two sites—in the City of Melbourne and the Cranbourne gardens. The 38-hectare Melbourne Gardens was founded in 1846 when land was reserved on the south side of the Yarra River for a new botanic garden.

pois.name: Westgate Park
pois.intro: Westgate Park is a public park in Port Melbourne, Victoria, 6 km southwest of the Melbourne central business district and covering 40 hectares of land. The park is located near Fishermans Bend, an industrial district along the left banks of the lower Yarra River downstream of the Maribyrnong River confluence, and is namesaked for the West Gate Bridge that traverses over the park's southern end.

pois.name: Fitzroy Gardens
pois.description: Victorian-era landscaped garden. Named after Sir Charles Augustus Fitzroy (1796-1858), Governor of New South Wales (1846-1851) and Governor-General of the Australian Colonies (1851-1855).
pois.intro: The Fitzroy Gardens is a 26-hectare urban park located south-east of the city centre of Melbourne in East Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. The gardens are bounded by Clarendon Street, Albert Street, Lansdowne Street, and Wellington Parade with the Treasury Gardens across Lansdowne street to the west.

pois.name: Batman Park
pois.intro: Batman Park is an urban park, located on the northern bank of the Yarra River in central Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Batman Park is a small open grassed space with paths and planted Eucalyptus trees bordered by Spencer Street at the west, Flinders Street Viaduct at the north and King Street to the east.

pois.name: Flagstaff Gardens
pois.intro: The Flagstaff Gardens is a 7.2-hectare urban park located in the city centre of Melbourne, in Victoria, Australia. Established in 1862, and formally reserved in 1873, the gardens are the oldest public park and are one of the most visited parks in the city, accessed by residents, nearby office workers, and tourists.

pois.name: Como House and Garden
pois.description: The gardens of Como House. Access to the gardens is free.
pois.intro: Como House is a historical house, with associated gardens in the City of Stonnington, Victoria, Australia. It was constructed in 1847 for Sir Edward Eyre Williams and now serves as a tourist attraction under the custodianship of the National Trust of Australia.

pois.name: Rippon Lea Estate
pois.intro: Rippon Lea Estate is a heritage-listed historic house and gardens located in Elsternwick, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. It is in the care of the National Trust of Australia.

pois.name: Pioneer Women's Memorial Garden
pois.intro: The Pioneer Women's Memorial Garden is located in Kings Domain, Melbourne, Australia and honours the contribution of women settlers to the development of the state of Victoria. In 1933, plans for the celebrations for the 1934 Centenary of Melbourne began to be made, and a Women's Centenary Council was formed to ensure women's opinions were included.

pois.name: St Kilda Beach
pois.intro: St Kilda Beach is a beach located in St Kilda, Port Phillip, Victoria, Australia, 6 kilometres south from the Melbourne city centre. It is Melbourne's most famous beach.

pois.description: HQ of National Trust of Australia (Victoria)

pois.name: La Trobe’s Cottage
pois.intro: La Trobe's Cottage is a historic cottage in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, built in 1839 by the first superintendent of the Port Phillip District of New South Wales, Charles La Trobe, and his family.

pois.name: Princess Theatre
pois.intro: The Princess Theatre, originally Princess's Theatre, is a 1452-seat theatre in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Established in 1854 and rebuilt in 1886 to a design by noted Melbourne architect William Pitt, it is the oldest surviving entertainment site on mainland Australia.

pois.name: Fiona & Sidney Myer Gallery
pois.description: The Fiona and Sidney Myer Gallery (formerly the Margaret Lawrence Gallery) is a highly influential curatorial art space frequented by the general public and artists at all stages of their career.
